text:
[LGRA.5.8.7] **A `Json` object names each key once.** JSON text in which one
object has two members with the same key is malformed. A runtime **must**
refuse such text wherever it parses JSON text, whoever supplies it, as it
refuses any other malformed text: a host call that parses it returns
`DS_ERR_PARSE` ([NERR.5]) and changes nothing. A runtime **must not** keep one
of the two members and drop the other.

Two keys are the same key when their strings are equal once escapes are
resolved, compared as UTF-8 bytes: `"a"` and `"\u0061"` are one key.

A recording read on replay whose `Json` value has an object with a repeated key
is a malformed atom body, and the runtime refuses the stream.

idris.name: Lgra_5_8_1__json
idris.note: The type carries no uniqueness index: `lgra_5_8_7__keys_unique` decides the clause's condition and the fixture runner refuses a document that fails it, so every document the model runs on names each key once. The refusal with DS_ERR_PARSE, and on replay, is the runtime's.

idris.name: lgra_5_8_7__keys_once
idris.note: Whether a list of keys names each once.

idris.name: lgra_5_8_7__keys_unique
idris.note: Whether every object in a document names each of its keys once: the clause's condition, decided. Keys are tokens of one string table, so two keys are the same key when their text is; escapes are resolved by the JSON parse that interns them.

idris.name: lgra_5_8_7__keys_unique_list
idris.note: The walk over an array's elements.

idris.name: lgra_5_8_7__keys_unique_members
idris.note: The walk over an object's members' values.
